messages:
maria: heads-up — ap-southeast2 nodes (scratchpool cohort c-17) started throwing CRC checks on /dev/nvme0n1 around 03:20 UTC, GPU attach requests are being held. nvme-bot posted some alerts below. :frowning_face:

nvme-bot: ALERT rc=1 host=c-17-03 metric=nvme_crc_count delta=+124 window=5m threshold=50 — auto-flagged nodes: [c-17-03, c-17-07, c-17-12]

jake_infra: thanks, looking. are these full host-level read errors or transient counters? can you paste a quick dmesg snippet?

maria: pasted below — intermittent read-retry then CRC reported by kernel, nodes still reachable but attach latency jumps to 15-30s and then k8s puts pods in Pending because the local ephemeral attach times out.

--- log ---
[03:19:42] nvme0n1: read error, retrying (status: 0x2)
[03:19:44] nvme0n1: CRC mismatch, bad block acknowledged
[03:20:03] nvme0n1: SMART Critical Warn: 0x2
--- end ---

lina_sre: if attachment latency > 10s we should stop scheduling new GPU pods there. suggests temporarily cordoning the nodes and letting the janitor finish scrub window. we can also reduce janitor concurrency to ease IO.

jake_infra: agree. plan: 1) cordon c-17-* 2) mark scratchpool as degraded in provisioner so GPU scheduler reroutes to reserved pool 3) lower janitor parallelism `--janitor-max-concurrency=4` for c-17 cohort. i'll run the commands.

sam_ops: quick cost check — routing to reserved pool adds ~2.6x tokenized unit cost for affected minutes, but replacing drives is a capital cost + logistics. what's the expected time-to-heal?

maria: initial estimate: if it's a scrub + transient retries, 1–4 hours with lowered janitor concurrency. if SMART keeps going up we'll need to proactively retire 3 drives which is a 48–72h full replacement/validation.

lina_sre: suggestion: do the software mitigations first (cordon, throttle janitor, fall back routing) and run `nvme smart-log` every 5m to confirm trend. if CRC continues to climb after 2 scrub cycles escalate to hardware retire.

jake_infra: running commands now: `kubectl cordon c-17-03 && kubectl drain c-17-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then patching provisioner: `kubectl -n infra patch cm scratchpool-config -p '{"data":{"max_concurrency":"4","degraded":"true"}}'`

maria: done cordon/drain on 03 and 07. started an isolated scrub on 12 (to avoid causing cluster-wide IO).

nvme-bot: NOTE host=c-17-12 scrub=started window=isolated reason=manual-trigger by maria

sam_ops: ok. cost-wise route-to-reserved for ~2–3h looks cheaper than immediate RMA shipping and SLA hit. but if we hit repeated CRC spikes across >20% of cohort we have to open a hardware batch order. I'll start an inventory check on spare nvme pool.

lina_sre: also adding a temporary autoscaler policy tweak: prioritize preemptible fallbacks to keep latency-sensitive workloads alive while we block scheduling onto degraded nodes.

jake_infra: follow-up checklist i pushed to infra runbook: - monitor nvme smart attr 0x12 (CRC) - metric alert lowered to 30/min for this cohort - rollback janitor concurrency after window - schedule RMA if SMART fails 2/3 cycles

maria: keeping an eye, will post a summary when scrub completes. ping me if GPU attach backlog > 45m. :thumbsup:

sam_ops: thanks — if backlog grows let's notify sales/customers for affected region as a precaution.

lina_sre: agreed. updating incident channel if we cross thresholds.

maria: scrub finished on c-17-12, CRC delta normalized to +3 in last 10m. uncordoning c-17-12 now. will leave 03/07 cordoned until we see stable SMART for 30m.

jake_infra: uncordon done for 12. rolling monitoring to 1m granularity for the next 2h.

sam_ops: closing provisional cost action — estimated extra infra cost ~USD 120 for reserved routing window. open hw-order if repeats.

maria: summary: software mitigation worked for now, two hosts under watch, will open hardware ticket if counters rise again. end of thread.
